label: Byaslag
step: heat to foam, add fermented milk, press
note: Also made from the milk left after making oerom; mostly cow and yak, sheep and goat milk go mostly into tea and cheese

about.text: A Mongolian cheese made by adding fermented milk to foaming heated milk, straining the curds through cloth and pressing them under a stone.

how.text: No species or temperatures are given by the source. IRCI calls byaslag the soft cheese and eezgii the dried one.

steps.note: Gentle flame, the milk ladled to foam.
A fermented milk of the tarag type is added to the foaming milk.

steps.name: strain
steps.note: The curds are strained through cloth.

steps.name: press
steps.note: Wrapped and pressed under a stone.

processing.text: A fermented milk (tarag-type) is added to gently heated, foaming milk; the curds are then strained and pressed. No species or temperatures are given.
